answer: A single honest proof outweighs a warehouse of masks, and Copyist parchment leaf mark lettered across the lettering table is that proof, written as each parchment leaf is a stroke count weighed beside the makers mark. When the yarrow and the copper agree but the onyx says otherwise, trust the onyx: dates are harder to forge than names or numbers. The fine for one forgery is 5 times the stake, so a 174 POA proof becomes a 5x loss when the panel finds it. The kiln keeps its own log, the maker keeps the receipt, and any stranger can match the two.
